Event Details
Participant Resources
Thank you for being part of the fal x Sequoia 72-Hour Video Hack 👋 This document contains all the key details you’ll need to make the most of the event.

1. Discord Server Information

3. Hackathon Rules
To keep things fair and aligned with our goals, all teams must follow these rules:

New Work Only: All projects must be started from scratch during the hackathon with no previous work.

Team Size: Teams may have up to 4 members.

Banned Projects: Projects will be disqualified if they: violate legal, ethical, or platform policies, use code, data, or assets you do not have the rights to.

[Generative Media Track]  Video Submissions – Content & IP

No third-party IP or non-consensual use of third-party IP. This includes close, high-fidelity imitations of real people — celebrities, gaming personalities, other public figures — or of copyrighted characters, whether by likeness, voice, or otherwise.

Inspiration, satire, and parody are fine. Drawing stylistically on a film, TV show, or other aesthetic is allowed, as are satire and parody — as long as they stay compliant with fal’s AUP (Acceptable Use Policy).

Nothing explicit. No gore, graphic violence, hate speech, promotion of violence, or sexual imagery.

4. Tracks & Themes
This hackathon is designed to showcase creativity in generative media, and build tools which help advance creatives within the space.

[Generative Media Track]  submit a maximum 3 minute AI-generated video under one of the following themes:

Film & Animation
 AI is transforming filmmaking. We want to see cinematic shorts that push storytelling, cinematography, and visual artistry.

Brand & Advertising
Create compelling brand campaigns, product films, or commercials that use AI to redefine how products and identities are brought to life.

Anime
Push the boundaries of AI-native anime through original worlds, unforgettable characters, and dynamic visual storytelling.

Open
Anything that doesn't fit the categories above. Surprise us with bold ideas, unconventional formats, and limitless creativity.


[Developer Track]  submit a GitHub repository along with a maximum 3 minute demo video showing what you built.

Build applications, tools, or workflows that make creating, editing, or producing AI-generated video faster, easier, or more powerful.

5. Build with fal
Participants will be provided with $100 in fal credits to be used throughout the hackathon. 

If you have not yet redeemed your credits, please contact us in Discord.

You can access partner tools, such as Grok, Google’s Gemini models, and Kling through the fal API.

Credit redemption instructions will be made available when hacking begins.

7. Judging
Judging for the fal x Sequoia 72-Hour Video Hack happens in two stages:

Stage 1 – Asynchronous Judging (Day 3)
Date & Time: July 19th, 9:00 AM PT / 12:00 PM ET

How it works:

Judges review your submitted projects asynchronously via the CV judging platform.

Each team will have uploaded:

A short demo video (3 minute maximum)

Written summary (100–200 words)

Judges independently evaluate projects using standardized criteria:



[Generative Media Track]

Creative vision / originality / art direction (30%) — Is the concept fresh and distinctive? Strong aesthetic point of view — cohesive visual style, color, composition, and tone that feel intentional rather than default model output.

Storytelling (35%) — Does the video have a clear narrative arc or emotional through-line? Pacing, structure, and payoff — does it hold attention and land its ending?

Technical capability (20%) — Visual consistency across shots (characters, environments, style), clean editing and transitions, sound design and music that elevate the piece.

Effective use of AI (15%) — Show how you used AI — which tools, where in the pipeline, and how you pushed them beyond obvious use. Clever workflows and prompt craft count.



[Developer Track]

Creativity (25%) — Novelty of the idea or approach — does it do something new, or tackle a familiar problem in an unexpected way?

User value (25%) — Does it solve a real problem for a real user? Clear target audience, intuitive UX, and plausible reason someone would use it again.

Technical execution (35%) — How difficult is this project to recreate? Does this involve technicality beyond your average hackathon project? Are you impressed with what they built in such a short time? 

Demo (15%) — How is the actual demo of the project? Does it impress you? Is it well-engineered and working?

After evaluation, the CV team aggregates scores to determine the top 6 projects for the final round

Stage 2 – Final Round Live Judging (Day 3)
Date & Time: July 19th,  7:00 PM PT / 10:00 PM ET

Format:

The top 6 projects will be announced on Discord.

Judges will watch each team’s video live and comment thoughts.

Judges will deliberate after all demos to determine the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners.
